dish.title: Maple Mustard Glazed Salmon
dish.name: Maple Mustard Glazed Salmon
dish.description: Salmon fillets roasted with a maple-Dijon glaze until the center reaches 145 F, with asparagus roasted beside them and a lemon-dill finish.

recipe.provenance_note: Legacy menu text of unknown origin. This draft reconciles that text. It does not claim a kitchen test.

recipe_version.title: Maple Mustard Glazed Salmon
recipe_version.description: Salmon fillets roasted with a maple-Dijon glaze until the center reaches 145 F, with asparagus roasted beside them and a lemon-dill finish.
recipe_version.serving_basis_note: Quantities are for 4 servings. One- and two-serving floors are not in this draft.
recipe_version.heat: Oven 425 F, then a short broil.
recipe_version.doneness: Cook the salmon to 145 F in the thickest part (FDA seafood guidance: https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/selecting-and-serving-fresh-and-frozen-seafood-safely). The center is opaque and the fish flakes. Rest 3 minutes. A thin fillet does not need to be pulled early for carryover.

ingredients.name: salmon fillets
ingredients.note: About 6 oz each, 1.5 lb total. Skin-on or skinless.

ingredients.name: Dijon mustard
ingredients.note: Store-bought. Not a dairy food in this catalog.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the asparagus, 1 tbsp in the glaze.

ingredients.name: lemon
ingredients.note: Zest in the glaze, 1 tbsp juice in the reserved glaze, the rest as wedges.

ingredients.name: fresh dill
ingredients.note: Chopped. Chives work if dill is out.

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.note: Divided: 5 g on the salmon, 2 g on the asparagus, 1 g in the glaze. 8 g Diamond Crystal kosher salt (2.75 tsp). The same weight is 1.75 tsp Morton coarse kosher salt or 1.25 tsp table salt. UC ANR publication 390575 (November 2023): Diamond Crystal kosher salt 2.8 g per teaspoon, Morton coarse kosher salt 4.8 g per teaspoon, table salt 6 g per teaspoon.

ingredients.name: black pepper
ingredients.note: Divided between the salmon and the asparagus.

steps.title: Heat the oven and season
steps.body: Heat the oven to 425 F with a rack in the upper third. Pat the salmon fillets dry. Season them with 5 g of the Diamond Crystal kosher salt and most of the black pepper.

steps.title: Season the asparagus
steps.body: Toss the asparagus with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 2 g of the Diamond Crystal kosher salt, and the rest of the black pepper. Do not brush the glaze onto the asparagus, because the glaze is for the salmon and would make the stalks sticky instead of roasted.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.body: Whisk the Dijon mustard, maple syrup, grated garlic, the lemon zest, the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, and the remaining 1 g Diamond Crystal kosher salt. Set aside 2 tbsp of this glaze for the finish.

steps.title: Roast and broil
steps.body: Roast the salmon fillets and the asparagus on a sheet pan at 425 F until the thickest part of the salmon is 145 F, opaque in the center, and flakes, about 8 to 12 minutes. Broil 1 to 3 minutes, watching, until the glaze spots amber. Rest 3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Whisk 1 tbsp lemon juice into the reserved glaze and spoon it over the salmon. Scatter the fresh dill and serve the remaining lemon as wedges.

recipe_version.dietary_label_note: Dairy-free. Dijon and maple syrup are not dairy. Not plant and not vegetarian. fish and finfish are not dietary labels. No wheat ingredient is listed. Gluten-free is not claimed.
allergen_notes: Dijon is not an allergen token here and it is not dairy.
No egg, milk, soy, wheat, sesame, peanut, tree_nut, or shellfish in the named foods.

culinary_revision.dietary: Still finfish only. Dairy-free. No new allergen. HH001 may eat finfish; eligibility booleans are unchanged.
culinary_revision.safety: Default doneness is 145 F internal per FDA. No lower pull temperature is given.

culinary_revision.uncertainties: Broil time depends on the oven. Dill versus chives is a cook's choice of one herb, not a stack of garnishes.
